title: Illegal crypto-based currency swaps total $2.2B, with 99% of defendants convicted
summary: An analysis of 52 cases involving digital assets used in violations of South Korea’s Foreign Exchange Transactions Act found that the total scale of the crimes reached about 3.1 trillion won ($2.2 billion), excluding acquittals, Digital Asset reported.According to the outlet, 17 of the 52 cases involved digital assets being used to mediate exchanges between the Chinese yuan and the South Korean won, the largest category. Illegal remittance cases involving Vietnam ranked second with 13 cases, while seven cases each were tied to the Philippines and casinos, and to swap crimes targeting the kimchi premium. Four other cases involved gift certificates, duty-free goods and so-called suitcase traders, while others included XRP exchange and small-sum overseas remittance cases.Of 95 defendants in total, including 93 individuals and two corporations, only one was ultimately acquitted. Among the 94 convicted defendants, 46, or 48.9%, received suspended prison terms, 28, or 29.7%, were fined, 19, or 20.2%, received prison sentences, and one, or 1.0%, received a suspended sentence for a fine. more:

title: Coinbase CEO says BTC price is driven by inflation fears, not mining
summary: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said on X that BTC price moves in line with inflation concerns. He said the hash power or energy devoted to mining does not determine BTC price, and even if miners exit, network difficulty adjusts to keep block production at the same pace. Over the long term, Armstrong said, BTC price is closer to an indicator of how much people worry about inflation, adding those concerns are unlikely to fade easily as fiscal deficits persist across democratic countries.Earlier, former Facebook executive Chamath Palihapitiya had argued that energy used for Bitcoin mining is shifting to AI as AI investment expands.
author: @CoinnessGL

title: Binance to end MOVR, GLMR mainnet support and migrate to Base
summary: Binance announced it will end support for the Moonriver (MOVR) and Moonbeam (GLMR) legacy mainnets and migrate the tokens to the Base network. According to the announcement, deposits and withdrawals of MOVR and GLMR via the Moonriver and Moonbeam mainnets will be suspended starting at 11:00 a.m. UTC on July 21. After the migration is completed, deposits and withdrawals through the Moonriver and Moonbeam mainnets will no longer be supported.
